answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity a bonded mooring, not a free key. Each agent berths at the registry jetty and posts a stake slashed if peers disprove its work; minting a thousand keys is free, but funding a thousand independent stakes scales linearly while marginal reward does not. A metered inlet keyed to the bond throttles sock puppets to near-zero throughput until probation ends. Subnetworks exchange tasks over a bridge that accepts only attestations countersigned by bonded peers, exposing self-dealing rings as cliques of idle accounts. Sybils persist, unprofitable.
